day_shape: 81 items: France publicly blames IRGC for supermarket refrigerator cyberattacks and summons Tehran's ambassador, Canada reimposes sanctions on 11 Iranian entities, US pulls aircraft from RAF Mildenhall over Iran threat, IRGC unveils new underground missile city, Trump calls war 'effectively over' while Qatar mediates.

threads.label: France-Iran cyberattack fallout
threads.summary: France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot accused Iran's Revolutionary Guards of cyberattacks that disrupted refrigerators at around 700 supermarkets, summoned Tehran's ambassador and announced plans for EU sanctions. Iran's Foreign Ministry rejected the accusations as baseless, while Iran's Human Rights Headquarters issued a counter-statement condemning French police handling of protests and the detention of 448 people.

threads.label: Trump-Iran war diplomacy via Doha
threads.summary: Trump said the Iran war was 'effectively over' militarily but US forces remained 'locked and loaded', as Qatar's prime minister held a 45-minute White House meeting on mediation and Turkey flagged planned high-level US-Iran talks in Doha. Rubio told G7 foreign ministers in Paris the US would keep imposing 'devastating' costs on Iran, and War Secretary Hegseth said he 'would do it again'.

threads.label: Canada sanctions and OFAC actions
threads.summary: Canada reimposed sanctions on 11 Iranian entities, including the national oil and tanker companies and four major banks previously delisted under the 2016 nuclear deal, citing nuclear and ballistic missile program support. FinCEN issued a special measure against MEXC Global and OFAC published updates to sanctions list entries.

threads.label: IRGC missile city unveiling
threads.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards unveiled a new underground missile facility in the presence of Chief of Staff General Ali Abdollahi and IRGC Aerospace Force commander Seyyed Majid Mousavi. Defa Press quoted Abdollahi saying Iran 'will certainly annihilate Israel' and promising battlefield 'surprises'.

threads.label: UK base evacuation and IDF escalation planning
threads.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported the US military moved tankers and tiltrotor aircraft out of RAF Mildenhall over an Iran threat, the second British base thinned out since a suspected Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford in September. The Jerusalem Post reported the IDF is preparing for two major escalation scenarios involving Iran.

threads.label: Gaza winter aid and Board of Peace
threads.summary: The IDF and COGAT said more than 91,000 tents and 8,200 trucks of winter supplies have entered Gaza under a plan coordinated with the Board of Peace, UN and international organisations. Trump's Board of Peace urged Israel to let in further winter supplies, calling flooding an immediate humanitarian emergency.

threads.label: Iran domestic rights crackdowns
threads.summary: Iran's judiciary announced arrests on a Tehran cultural street over hijab defiance and sealed multiple restaurants for allegedly failing to observe Islamic norms, while a Tehran gynecologist faces prosecution over public comments about single motherhood. UN human rights experts warned of escalating persecution of independent lawyers, and Iran Human Rights said detained lawyer Amirsalar Davoudi suffered a heart attack in custody.

events.summary_en: Peacekeepers in the ranks of war Military exercises by European troops in Poland and the promise of their deployment in Ukraine after the end of the war with Russia makes the challenging path to peace longer. These exercises are being held on the eve of peace talks between Russia, the United States, and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi. The main question is why European countries are planning for the deployment of their own military forces in Ukraine at such a juncture and what objectives the leaders of these countries pursue through this action. Britain, France, and several other European countries have decided that after the end of hostilities with Russia, reliable security guarantees outside the NATO framework will be made available to Kyiv.

The enemy, through investment and establishing surveillance networks around prominent schools and universities, seeks to attract and remove talented human capital. Confronting this process requires identification, organisation, team-building, and comprehensive support for students and university students.
